name: Beirut Rafic Hariri International Airport
before:
Lebanon's only working commercial airport, in the southern suburbs of Beirut 9 km from the centre. It is the hub for Middle East Airlines and, along with the Port of Beirut, the country's main point of entry.

The terminal is U shaped, with an East and a West Wing joined by the main building, and has 23 gates, 19 of them with jetways. There is a three level car park holding 2,350 cars.

Ground transport is the part to prepare a client for. There is no public transport to the terminal itself, only taxis, and airport taxis cost more than the ordinary service taxis in the city. The nearest buses stop at the airport roundabout a kilometre away, where LCC route 1 runs to Rue Sadat in Hamra and route 5 to the Charles Helou bus station. Arrange a transfer in advance.

The airport is run directly by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation, which also controls Lebanese airspace. It was named after Rafic Hariri in 2005, the year the former prime minister was assassinated.
after:
Lebanon's only airport with commercial flights, in Beirut's southern suburbs 9 km from the centre. It is the base for Middle East Airlines.

According to the FCDO, the airport is open and operational, but travellers should check the local security situation before going there. The FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Beirut and its southern suburbs, though not to Route 51 from central Beirut to the airport. Israeli air strikes hit the southern suburbs in 2026, and the FCDO says fighting and strikes have continued since a cessation of hostilities was announced in June, particularly in southern Lebanon. Arrange a transfer in advance.

The airport is run by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation, which also provides air traffic control for Lebanese airspace. It was renamed in 2005 after Rafic Hariri, the assassinated former prime minister.

claims.note: Was 'only working commercial airport'. Still true in September 2026, but only just: a second airport, René Mouawad at Qlayaat in the north, was officially inaugurated on 6 June 2026 (AGBI, Al Jazeera, Beirut.com) and its operator said on 14 September that it has not yet begun commercial operations (LBCI). The Qlayaat opening is not added to the text because it would be a new fact; flagged for the owner.
